html:
The Battle of Tricamarum was fought on 15 December 533 about 30 kilometres west of Carthage, in today's Tunisia. The Byzantine general Belisarius beat the Vandal king Gelimer and ended the Vandal Kingdom.

The emperor Justinian wanted to win back the western lands of the old Roman Empire, and sent Belisarius to Africa with about 15,000 men. In September Belisarius won at Ad Decimum and took Carthage. Gelimer gathered his remaining forces, called his brother Tzazo back from Sardinia, and camped at Tricamarum. Belisarius marched out to meet him. The fight was almost all cavalry. Twice the Byzantine horsemen charged across a small stream and were pushed back. The third charge broke the Vandal centre and killed Tzazo. Gelimer lost heart and fled, and his army fell apart.

Gelimer gave himself up a few months later and was led through Constantinople in a triumph. The Vandalic War had lasted less than a year. North Africa stayed under the Byzantine Empire until the Arab conquests of the late 600s, and its quick fall encouraged Justinian to invade Italy next. The source is Procopius, who was there. The exact site is not known.
